sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and fake facts
sections.what: Creates 35 fake facts that all quote the same sentence, each with its own link and a verified check, so the tests can check page splitting and citations.
sections.why: A large number of facts is used to test that long lists are split across pages without losing any.
sections.watch_out: The facts are invented, so a passing test does not show that real sources are correct.

sections.name: recipe
sections.title: Fake run and the two tests
sections.what: Builds a small fake run with two projects, one theme and one assessment, then builds its slides. The first test checks passages, excluded projects, unique page IDs, page order and citations. The second test writes a PowerPoint file and reads its text back to compare with the stored pages.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms that the content builder and the PowerPoint writer agree on what each slide says.
sections.watch_out: The second test calls python3, so it can fail on a machine without it for reasons unrelated to the code.

summary: Tests that the content builder keeps every supporting passage and citation, and that the PowerPoint writer stores the same pages in the same order.
purpose: Protects the lessons-learnt content and PowerPoint output from silent regressions.
why: Reason not stated in the code, but the test names describe the rules the content must keep.
how: Builds 35 fake facts that quote the same sentence, plus a small fake run with two projects, one contributing and one excluded. Test one checks that every passage is present, the excluded project is absent, page IDs are unique and each slide has one citation per bullet. Test two writes a PowerPoint file, reads the text from each slide, and checks the titles and bullets match the stored pages.
inputs: Fixture data defined in this file only. No live database or network is used.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the node test runner.
risks: The fixtures are invented, so passing tests show that the code handles this shape of data, not that real data is correct. The second test depends on python3 being installed.
debug: If the first test fails, look for the missing fact or page named in the assertion message. If the second test fails, check that python3 is available and that the page count matches the slide count. Failures on text matching often come from whitespace differences.
